facts.text: Coconut Grove, founded in 1825 when the Cape Florida lighthouse opened, is Miami’s oldest continuously inhabited neighborhood.
The definitive spelling “Coconut Grove” was adopted in 1919 when Miami incorporated the area, replacing earlier variations like “Cocoanut Grove.”.
English immigrants Isabella and Charles Peacock built the Bay View Inn in 1882, which later became the Peacock Inn on today’s Peacock Park.
Black Bahamian immigrants helped construct historic landmarks, and the neighborhood now celebrates its heritage at sites like Macedonia Missionary Baptist Church and Coconut Grove Cemetery.
The Goombay festival, a celebration of Coconut Grove’s rich Bahamian history, draws crowds each year to honor its cultural roots.
The Village Center, centered on Main, McFarland, and Grand Avenues, houses CocoWalk’s multiplex, a state historic site, and the Coconut Grove Post Office, making it a local hub.
